'''Richard John Samworth''' (born May 1978) is a British statistician who is the [[Professor of Statistical Science (Cambridge)|Professor of Statistical Science]] and the [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge#Directors of the Statistical Laboratory|Director]] of the [[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge]],<ref name="cam">{{cite web|url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Dept/People/samworth.html |title=Richard Samworth {{pipe}} Official web page at Cambridge |publisher=statslab.cam.ac.uk|accessdate=21 June 2016}}</ref> and a Teaching Fellow of [[St John's College, Cambridge]]. He was educated at [[St John's College, Cambridge]]. His main research interests are in [[nonparametric statistics|nonparametric]] and [[high-dimensional statistics]]. Particular topics include shape-constrained [[density estimation]] and other nonparametric function estimation problems, nonparametric [[Statistical classification|classification]], [[cluster analysis|clustering]] and [[Nonparametric regression|regression]], the [[bootstrap (statistics)|bootstrap]] and high-dimensional [[variable selection]] problems.
